<!-- version: 2.61.0 -->
Monthly series can now repeat on the last day of the month, whatever length that month has. Until now this could only be approximated by starting a series on the 31st, and the approximation broke the first time it met a shorter month. The repetition form has a new choice under "monthly"; it is the one thing a start date cannot express by itself, because "the last day" is a different date every month. Existing series are untouched and keep repeating exactly as before - the new behaviour applies only where you pick it.

A yearly series on 29 February comes back in the next leap year. It used to drop to the 28th after the first ordinary year and stay there for good, so a birthday entered for 29 February was shown on the wrong day from the second year onwards and never returned. This is worth knowing before you update: an affected series will show a different date afterwards than it has been showing, and that date is the correct one. Nothing is re-entered and no database change is applied.

Two smaller repairs to repeating appointments. Choosing "this and all following" on the *first* appointment of a series could make the whole series disappear from the calendar while its entry stayed behind - that happened when a series began on a day its own rule does not contain, such as a weekly "Mondays only" starting on a Saturday, which is how some calendar apps write it. At the beginning of a series that choice now simply means the whole series. And a series limited to a number of repetitions and restricted to certain weekdays no longer ends early: days outside the weekday pattern were counted against the limit although they were never shown, so a series set to two appointments could deliver one.

Full release notes are available at https://github.com/ulsklyc/yuvomi/releases/tag/v2.61.0
